title: Partner listing acceptance criteria & launch contingency notes
content:
Purpose
- Capture precise acceptance criteria for partner marketplace listings plus practical contingency plans for launch day incidents. This is a working playbook: not everything final.

Scope
- Applies to: AWS/Azure/GCP marketplace listings, publisher-syndication channels, and any co-managed partner tiles. Not covering reseller billing or managed services SLA contracts (separate doc).

Top-level goals
- Tile published with correct entitlement mapping, trial metadata, price SKU match, and secure onboarding flow.
- Copy aligns to legal/marketing guardrails and technical integration passes QA.
- Launch risk mitigations defined with clear rollback triggers and owners.

Acceptance criteria (hard gates)
1) Copy & Marketing
   - Title <= 60 chars; one-line summary <= 140 chars. No unverified claims (eg: "best" or ranking claims) per legal.
   - Short tile copy produced (20–40 words), medium description (80–160 words), and long description (300–600 words). All three variants provided.
   - 3x asset images (1024x1024 preferred), 1x logo (512x512), 1x hero screenshot that matches published UI.
   - Trial language: explicit trial length, auto-conversion behavior, what features are trialed vs behind paid SKU.

2) Technical / Integration
   - OIDC SSO flow tested end-to-end (test user created in partner account).
   - Entitlement API responds 200/JSON and provisions sandbox workspace within <10s for test flows.
   - Billing SKU mapping validated with finance (SKU match + price point parity).
   - Container/VM image (if required) passes vulnerability scan (critical/ high = 0 unresolved).
   - Private deployments: KMS key exchange and network egress policy documented.

3) Legal & Security
   - DPA & standard T&Cs attached to listing and accessible in tile. Legal approval doc id noted.
   - Data handling statement present for user-provided data; PII flow diagram attached.
   - Minimum security controls: TLS 1.2+, RBAC mapping documented, audit logs retention policy set.

4) Observability & SLOs
   - Route-level latency baseline measured in staging and within 10% of production target.
   - Error budget and alert rules created in Redwood Console: 5xx rate >0.5% triggers paging.
   - Cost estimate per-seat / per-1000 tokens included for marketplace listing copy (to prevent surprises).

Preflight checklist (quick pass)
- [ ] Tile copy (short/medium/long) uploaded and approved
- [ ] Assets: logo, hero, screenshots uploaded
- [ ] Pricing + SKU mapping verified with finance
- [ ] Entitlement and trial behavior documented
- [ ] OIDC SSO tested (happy path + failure path)
- [ ] Billing integration smoke test (sandbox payment)
- [ ] Security review complete (attestation from sec team)
- [ ] Legal sign-off on copy and data statements
- [ ] Support runbook & escalation path added to tile
- [ ] Support alias created: partners-support+marketplace@redwood.ai

Launch day contingency plans (play-by-play)
- Immediate triage owner: Partnerships on-call (Ava Patel). Backup: Product Ops (Sofia Ramirez).
- Pager conditions (examples):
   - Publishing error -> roll back to previous draft (manual unpublish).
   - Trial provisioning failures > 5% of signups in 15m -> disable trial via backend feature flag (feature/entitlements toggle).
   - Billing SKU mismatch detected by customers -> unlist tile temporarily and notify channel #partners-launch + partner contact.
   - Security incident / data leakage -> follow incident response (sec on-call + legal); unpublish tile if leakage confirmed.

Rollback triggers (explicit)
- Severe user-impacting errors: any onboarding path returning 500 for >10% of attempts over 10m.
- Billing mismatch where charged price != marketplace price.
- Verified data exposure outside contractual boundaries.
- If rollback: 1) Unpublish listing, 2) Open incident in JIRA, 3) Notify partner and internal stakeholders, 4) Run postmortem 48–72h.

Messaging bank (copy variants)
- Tile short: "Redwood Inference — predictable, low-latency LLM inference for production apps."
- Tile medium: "Run LLM inference with predictable latency and cost across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Try a 14-day trial with instant sandbox provisioning."
- Tile long (skeleton): "Redwood Inference helps engineering teams ship LLM features that meet production requirements — throughput, latency, cost control, and private deployment options. Our platform supports hosted APIs, reserved dedicated capacity, and private VPC installs, with observability and rollout tools to keep your app reliable at scale. Learn more and start a sandbox trial today."
- Social/PR snippet: "Redwood Inference now available on [Marketplace]. Fast onboarding, dedicated capacity, and enterprise-ready controls. Try a sandbox now."

Pricing / entitlement sketches (notes)
- Option A: metered tokens billed via marketplace (parity price). Trial: 200k tokens free.
- Option B: seat + reserved throughput: monthly reserved capacity SKU (commit). Trial: 14-day credit applied to reserved pool.
- Finance checkpoint required: confirm tax handling + marketplace commission impact on price.

QA tests to run (staging -> prod smoke)
- Smoke 1: Create account via marketplace tile -> verify onboarding flow completes and sandbox appears within expected time.
- Smoke 2: Generate sample inference request with test prompt; assert latency < 300ms p50 for small sequences.
- Smoke 3: Embed API call for trial account; verify token counts decrement and no overage billing occurs during trial.
- Smoke 4: SSO SAML/OIDC sign-in and sign-out flows validated for partner org.
- Smoke 5: Entitlement revoke test: revoke entitlement and verify access removed within 60s.

Support & escalation matrix
- Tier 1: Partner success (partners-support@redwood.ai) handles initial inbound and collects logs.
- Tier 2: Solutions Eng (on-call) performs repro and targeted debugging.
- Tier 3: Serving runtime + infra paged for production issues.
- Contact list: Partner PM (name on partner contract), Partner Eng lead, Legal rep, Security rep.

Post-launch monitoring & KPIs (first 72h)
- Provisioning success rate (target >= 99%)
- Trial-to-convert rate (early signal)
- Errors by route (high freq routes flagged)
- Latency p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens observed vs estimate

Open questions / TODOs
- Confirm official legal blurb for third-party data usage (action: Sofia Ramirez, due 2025-02-18).
- Do we permit free-tier API keys to be listed in tile? Potential abuse vector. Decision needed. (ping #security)
- Need final hero screenshot reflecting new console UI (owner: Dmitri Kozlov).
- Validate marketplace-specific image spec for Azure (they require PNG with transparent background).

Notes to self / working items
- Keep copy variants short; marketplace truncation often kills messaging. Use 1–2 CTA variations.
- Avoid feature laundry list in short copy; emphasize outcome (latency, cost, privacy).
- Bookmark: Confluence page 'Marketplace pricing parity' for finance numbers.

Appendix: quick checklist for unpublish flow (operational)
1) Partner PM triggers unpublish request via partner console
2) Ops: toggle listing state to draft (internal tool)
3) Notify partner + create JIRA incident with "unpublish" tag
4) If rollback caused by code change, revert PR and schedule hotfix; if caused by misconfig, correct and re-validate staging.

Linked tickets / references
- JIRA: PLAT-876 (entitlements), PLAT-901 (billing parity), GO2MKT-452 (listing copy), SEC-199 (vuln scan exception workflow).
- Confluence: Marketplace launch playbook draft (internal)

-- end of working draft --
